pass_a_gloss: … you practised [the righteousness, with exactness]), but so that you might appear. Let us not be shown up unjust, nor impious. Let us remember these things in the times of hardships, and let us seem (think) to hear God being present and saying to us: Do you think that I have given you a divine answer (dealt with you) otherwise than so that to those not knowing your righteousness may become plain? Label: verse 5 (LXX numbering; KJV 40:10). Take up now height and power, and put glory and honour around yourself. Crown yourself, put on glory, put on honour, put on comeliness. The insolent one campaigned against you; but you humbled the proud one, and turned back his phalanxes far off with shame. Refute sinners, showing them sinners; fill their faces with dishonour, through the refutation that is in you. Not then for display, or toward also all the other things, or also toward knowledge of God (sense obscure). See how much he refutes him on the lowliness of his nature, and does not say that you are lowly, but that I am great, and he is not able for the things which I am. Label: verse 10 (KJV 40:15). But now behold beasts beside you. As an athlete, learn the things about the dragon, the antagonist. Beside you then, he says, and beside every enduring person these beasts are tamed and have been subjected; there is however, etc. Label: verse 20 (KJV 41:1). You will lead a dragon on a hook, you will put a halter around his nose? Are you able then, he says, O Job, to do what the Only-begotten afterwards worked? For as if putting forward his own flesh to him as a certain bait, through his own nails, as through hooks, he hunted the fish Leviathan. For so the Hebrew has it, and it signifies the dragon. Label: verse 27 (KJV 41:8). Will you lay a hand on him, having remembered the war happening in his body [and let it no longer happen]? War here he calls the disturbance, the wildness, his dashing against. How does it happen, he says? Such is the beast, wild and powerful and stricken senseless. Can you, he says, by your power bind him down? or at all remember and think of the war that is going to happen in his body? His body he calls demons, as he is head of them; and this war the Lord conquered through the trophy of the cross. And the 'let it no longer happen', since the cross has happened once; for who died to sin, he says, died once and for all. Chapter 41, verse 4 (KJV 41:13). Who will uncover the face of his clothing? pass_b_english: … practised), but “that you might be made manifest.” Let us not be shown to be unjust, or ungodly. Let us remember these things in times of hardship, and let us think that we hear God, present with us and saying to us: “Do you think that I have dealt with you for any other reason than that your righteousness might become plain to those who do not know it?”

“Take up now loftiness and power, and clothe yourself in glory and honour” (Job 40:10). Crown yourself: put on glory, put on honour, put on comeliness. The insolent one made war on you, but you humbled the proud one and turned his ranks back far away in shame. Convict sinners by showing them to be sinners; fill their faces with dishonour through the proof that is in you. So it is not for display; or else it is for all the other things as well, or even for the knowledge of God. See how far he convicts Job of the lowliness of his nature: he does not say that you are lowly, but that I am great, and that he cannot do what I can.

“But now, behold, wild beasts are with you” (Job 40:15). As an athlete, learn about the dragon, your opponent. With you, then, he says, and with everyone who endures, these beasts are tamed and made subject. There is, however … and so on.

“Will you lead a dragon with a hook, and put a halter round his nose?” (Job 41:1). Can you, then, he says, O Job, do what the Only-begotten later accomplished? For he held out his own flesh to him as a kind of bait, and through his own nails, as through hooks, he caught the fish Leviathan. That is what the Hebrew has, and it means the dragon.

“Will you lay a hand on him, remembering the war that is waged in his body? And let it happen no more” (Job 41:8). By war he means here the turmoil, the savagery, his onrush. How can that be done? he says. Such is the beast: savage and powerful and senseless. Can you, he says, bind him down by your own strength? Or even so much as remember and conceive the war that is to be waged in his body? By his body he means the demons, since he is their head; and this war the Lord won through the trophy of the cross. And “let it happen no more” is said because the cross has taken place once; for “he who died to sin,” it says, “died once for all” (Romans 6:10).
“Who will uncover the face of his garment?” (Job 41:13).

lemmas.gloss: give a divine answer, deal with

choices.choice: Every clause retranslated from the locked Greek. Old errors fixed: 'hearing the glory of God' (δόξωμεν is 'let us think', from δοκέω); 'Do not allow yourself to appear' (ἀναφανῶμεν is first person plural); 'the lowly nature ... rebukes him' and 'I cannot do what you do' (God convicts Job of his lowliness; οὐ δύναται ἅπερ ἐγώ = he cannot do what I can); 'beasts are set against you' (παρὰ σοί = with you); 'so did Leviathan draw up the dragon' through his 'ribs' (the Only-begotten catches Leviathan through his nails, ἥλων); 'as if they were his head' (ὡς αὐτοῦ κεφαλὴ ὄντος = since he is their head); 'embittered state' for τὸ χρίμψασθαι (onrush).

Labels εʹ, ιʹ, κʹ, κζʹ (chapter 40) and ΜΑʹ δʹ follow the older LXX verse numbering; the lemma wording matches KJV Job 40:10, 40:15, 41:1, 41:8 and 41:13, so those English references are printed after each lemma.
οὐ λέγει ὅτι ταπεινὸς σὺ, ἀλλ' ὅτι μέγας ἐγὼ, καὶ οὐ δύναται ἅπερ ἐγώ moves from 'you' to 'he'; kept as indirect speech ('that he cannot do what I can') rather than smoothed.

Οὐκ ἄρα πρὸς ἐπίδειξιν ἢ πρὸς καὶ τὰ ἄλλα πάντα, ἢ καὶ πρὸς θεογνωσίαν is rendered closely ('So it is not for display; or else it is for all the other things as well, or even for the knowledge of God'); the second ἢ may mean 'than'. Meaning uncertain; no sense added.
'senseless' (LSJ: struck senseless, crazed); an active sense 'stunning' is possible.
[καὶ μηκέτι γινέσθω] is the editor's supplement of the lemma from the LXX; translated without brackets ('And let it happen no more') because the comment then expounds it.
Opens mid-sentence (the parenthesis '(for you practised righteousness with exactness)' begins in u02-rem-close); the final article Τὸ is translated as 'The' at the start of u03-rem-early.
Old text displayed 'Romans 6:10' but linked Hebrews 9:28. The quotation ὃς γὰρ ἀπέθανε τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ... ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ is Romans 6:10 (KJV 'he died unto sin once'); plain reference kept, link removed.
